Ippolito Cavalcanti, Duca di Buonvicino, Cucina teorico-pratica, with the
appendix "Cucina casarinola all'uso nuosto napolitano".

Source Internet Archive item IppolitoCavalcanti-CucinaTeorica-pratica
https://archive.org/details/IppolitoCavalcanti-CucinaTeorica-pratica
(user upload of a Google-digitised copy; uploader listed as a private
individual, item carries no date and no rights statement)
Accessed 2026-08-30

DATING -- established from internal evidence, not from the item metadata:
dedicatory letters dated "Napoli li 24 Giugno 1839" and "Napoli 25 Giugno 1839"
a reference to "ottobre dello scorso anno 1838"
=> this is the 1839 edition, the one that introduced the Neapolitan-dialect
appendix. DO NOT cite it as the 1837 first edition.
Rights Public domain: published 1839.

TWO PDFs ARE HELD -- USE THE SEARCHABLE ONE
*.pdf the item's default PDF. IMAGE-ONLY: 472 pp but only ~6,400
characters of text layer, and ZERO tomato hits. Do not
term-search this file; you will get false negatives.
*.searchable.pdf the item's "_text.pdf". Same 472 pp, ~612,000 characters,
90 pomidoro/pommadoro hits. Use this one.
*.ocr.txt the item's _djvu.txt OCR layer, used for the analysis.

Key passage, in the dialect appendix:
"Viermicielli co le pommadoro. Piglia quatto rotola de pommadoro, le taglie
ncroce, ne lieve la semmenta, e chella acquiccia, e le fai vollere; quanno se
sonco squagliate le passarraje pe lo setaccio, e chillo zuco lo farraje
stregnere ncoppa a lo fuoco..."
-- usually called the first pasta-with-tomato-sauce recipe.
Also records preserving for winter: "pomidoro secchi ... ovvero di quelle in
bottiglie" (dried, or bottled).
